Schefferville|Canada.f: Schefferville is named after Bishop Lionel Scheffer, Apostolic Vicar of Labrador from 1946 until his death in 1966.

Fort Chipewyan|Canada.f: Fur trader Roderick Mackenzie started a library here in 1790 with over 2,000 books and called the post the little Athens of the Arctic.

Burns Lake|Canada.f: In June 1982 Burns Lake logged 376.5 hours of sunshine, the most ever recorded in British Columbia for a June.

Lynn Lake|Canada.f: The town was created by moving 219 buildings from Sherridon by tractor train, a job that took four winters.

Coral Harbour|Canada.f: The Sadlermiut people of this area were wiped out by illness within weeks in 1902-03 and went culturally extinct.

Masset|Canada.f: Masset, on Haida Gwaii, has recorded wind gusts of 160 km/h (99 mph).

Spring Point|Bahamas.f: The Plana Cays off Acklins are a reserve for the Bahamian hutia, a guinea pig-like rodent, and for endangered iguanas.

Chub Cay|Bahamas.f: Chub Cay in the Berry Islands is described as the billfish capital of The Bahamas.

Pickle Lake|Canada.f: Named for a lake shaped like a pickle, it is the most northerly community in Ontario with year-round road access.

Port-Menier|Canada.f: Port-Menier on Anticosti Island was built in the late 19th century by French chocolate maker Henri Menier.

Blanc-Sablon|Canada.f: The area holds over 60 archaeological sites spanning 9,000 years of human occupation, a National Historic Site since 2007.

Îles-de-la-Madeleine|Canada.f: Jacques Cartier found these islands on June 25, 1534 and named them Iles de Margaulx after the many gannets.

Natashquan|Canada.f: Natashquan had no road link to the rest of Quebec until Route 138 was extended to Havre-Saint-Pierre in 1996.

Vieques|Puerto Rico.f: Vieques Bioluminescent Bay was named the brightest bioluminescent bay in the world by Guinness World Records in 2006.

Sint Eustatius|Caribbean Netherlands.f: On November 16, 1776 the island's governor answered a US warship with cannon fire, an early foreign salute to the American flag.

North Caicos|Turks and Caicos Is..f: North Caicos is the second-largest island in the Turks and Caicos Islands, after Middle Caicos.

Bella Coola|Canada.f: Alexander Mackenzie reached Bella Coola in 1793, completing the first recorded crossing of the continent north of Mexico.

Baker Lake|Canada.f: Baker Lake is the only inland community in Nunavut.

Marie-Galante|Guadeloupe.f: Because it is round and almost flat, the island is nicknamed la grande galette, the Big Biscuit.

Colonel Hill|Bahamas.f: Crooked Island is believed to have had the first post office in the Bahamas, at Pitts Town.

Andros Town|Bahamas.f: Andros has the world's largest collection of blue holes and a 225 km barrier reef, the world's sixth longest.

St. Anthony|Canada.f: L'Anse aux Meadows, the first and only known Viking site in North America, lies 40 km from St. Anthony.

Island Lake|Canada.f: A monument at the east end of Island Lake marks a key point on the Ontario-Manitoba boundary.

Moosonee|Canada.f: Moosonee has no road connection and is the railhead of the Polar Bear Express train from the south.

Deadman's Cay|Bahamas.f: Dean's Blue Hole on Long Island is the world's second deepest underwater sinkhole, dropping about 200 meters.

Stella Maris|Bahamas.f: Stella Maris was established as a resort in 1963 and has a year-round population of only about 80 people.

Nevis|St. Kitts and Nevis.f: The name comes from Nuestra Senora de las Nieves, Our Lady of the Snows, and Alexander Hamilton was born in Charlestown.

Kulusuk|Greenland.f: The village church was built in 1908 from the timbers of a Danish sailing ship that ran aground nearby.

Anahim Lake|Canada.f: Every July the Anahim Lake Stampede is the area's major social event.

Bella Bella|Canada.f: A 1997 Supreme Court of Canada ruling recognized the Heiltsuk of Bella Bella as having an Aboriginal right to commercial herring fishing.

Bequia|St. Vin. and Gren..f: Bequia islanders may catch up to four humpback whales a year, using only hand-thrown harpoons from small open sailboats.

Kasabonika|Canada.f: In the 1960s and 70s Kasabonika residents worked as tree planters, some planting as many as 3,000 trees a day.

Nakina|Canada.f: In World War II a radar base on the edge of Nakina watched for attacks on the locks at Sault Ste. Marie.

Sandy Lake|Canada.f: Sandy Lake is joined to the road network by a winter ice road meeting the Nungesser Road, which is open about six weeks a year.

Mustique|St. Vin. and Gren..f: Colin Tennant bought Mustique for 45,000 pounds in 1958 and gave Princess Margaret a plot there as a 1960 wedding present.

Virgin Gorda|British Virgin Is..f: Columbus is said to have named it Virgen Gorda, the fat virgin, because its profile looks like a woman lying on her side.

Aasiaat|Greenland.f: Aasiaat means spiders in Greenlandic, probably because spiders were abundant when the settlement was founded.

Sisimiut|Greenland.f: Sisimiut's Bethel Church, built in 1775, is described as the oldest surviving church in Greenland.

Culebra|Puerto Rico.f: Culebra's wildlife refuge, set up by Theodore Roosevelt on February 27, 1909, is one of the oldest bird sanctuaries in US territory.

Union Island|St. Vin. and Gren..f: Happy Island, a man-made island holding a bar, sits in the middle of Clifton harbour.
